exampleAnswers.title: Evaluating Trigonometric Ratios Given a Triangle with Integer Side Lengths

question.explanation:
The tangent of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the adjacent (T-O-A). Relative to the angle $ D,$ the opposite side is $\overline{BC},$ and the adjacent is $\overline{BD}.$ Therefore,

\[ \eqalign{ \tan{D} &= \dfrac{BC}{BD}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{8}{6}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{4}{3}. } \]

question.explanation:
The cosine of an angle is equal to the adjacent divided by the hypotenuse (C-A-H). Relative to the angle $ E,$ the adjacent side is $\overline{FE},$ and the hypotenuse is $\overline{DE}.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \cos{E} &= \dfrac{FE}{DE}=\dfrac{80}{89}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Evaluating a Trigonometric Ratio Given a Triangle with Non-Integer Side Lengths

question.explanation:
The cosine of an angle is equal to the adjacent divided by the hypotenuse (C-A-H). Relative to the angle $S,$ the adjacent side is $\overline{ST},$ and the hypotenuse is $\overline{SR}.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \cos{S} &= \dfrac{ {ST}}{{SR}} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{19}}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{19}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{19}}{\sqrt{19}} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{\sqrt{133}}{19}. \end{align*}

question.text: In the right triangle $\triangle ABC,$ $\angle A$ is a right angle, $AB=3\sqrt{7},$ $AC=9$ and $BC=12.$ Find $\sin C.$
question.explanation:
Let's illustrate the given triangle.

The sine of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the hypotenuse (S-O-H). Relative to the angle $C,$ the opposite side is $\overline{AB},$ and the hypotenuse is $\overline{CB}.$ Therefore,

\[ \eqalign{ \sin{C} &= \dfrac{AB}{CB} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{7}}{12} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{4}. } \]

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio

question.explanation:
The tangent of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the adjacent (T-O-A).

Relative to the angle $\theta,$ the length of the opposite side is $6x-5,$ and the length of the adjacent side is $4x.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \tan\theta&=\dfrac{\textrm{opposite}}{\textrm{adjacent}}\\[5pt] \dfrac{15}{12}&=\dfrac{6x-5}{4x}\\[5pt] 60x&=72x-60\\[5pt] 12x&=60\\[5pt] x&=5. \end{align*}

example.title: Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio

question.explanation:
The cosine of an angle is equal to the adjacent divided by the hypotenuse (C-A-H).

Relative to the angle $\theta,$ the length of the adjacent side is $\dfrac{7}{4}x + 29,$ and the length of the hypotenuse is $7x + 17.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \cos\theta&=\dfrac{\textrm{adjacent}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}\\[5pt] \dfrac{5}{8}&=\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{7}{4}x+29\right)}{7x+17}\\[5pt] 5(7x + 17) & = 8\left(\dfrac{7}{4}x + 29\right)\\[5pt] 35x+85&=14x+232\\[5pt] 21x&=147\\[5pt] x&=7. \end{align*}
